text: For example, we view Israel's settlements in the West Bank as illegal under international law and we think, in fact, proceeding with the way they have proceeded over the last couple of decades after the failure of the Oslo Accords, will only make things worse and make it much more difficult to arrive at a two-state solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we have voted in favour of every UN resolution that calls on Israel to rescind unilateral measures to change the status of Jerusalem, not because we have a view on how to settle the Jerusalem question, but because we believe this can only be done through direct negotiations between the two Semitic tribes, the Palestinians and the Israelis, directly arriving at a consensus, however long, however difficult that will be.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Zulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked how we have contributed to the humanitarian situation in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans actually have contributed generously with humanitarian assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our strong ties with our partners in the Middle East have allowed us to collaborate with them on the delivery of this aid.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So far, we have sent two tranches of life-saving aid for the civilians in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Minister Maliki was in Cairo in early November last year to personally hand over the first tranche to the Egyptian Red Crescent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A few weeks later we sent a second tranche that was delivered directly to El Arish, an airport in Egypt near the Egypt-Gaza border.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This was delivered by an RSAF, our military aircraft.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In January 2024, Members would know that we also sent an SAF medical team to serve on board a French Navy ship to treat casualties from Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue also our long-standing support for the Palestinian Authority's capacity-building efforts through our $10 million Enhanced Technical Assistance Package.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As I said before, we have good ties with the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee, Senior Minister Teo, Minister Maliki and I have visited Ramallah on multiple occasions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have met our counterparts there and even during this crisis I have been in phone contact with the Palestinian Authority Foreign Minister.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do all this because we look forward to the day when there is peace and that there is a functioning, capable Palestinian State and that the Palestinian people get the peace and progress which they so richly deserve.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I mentioned earlier we have also established a representative office in Ramallah in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, I appreciate that many Singaporeans feel deeply about what is happening.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I also hope you can understand my point that foreign policy cannot be driven one way or the other by sentiment or affinity to any external group.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our foreign policy must be based on understanding our core interests and acting consistently in accordance with the principles that safeguard our Independence, our sovereignty, our territorial integrity and our security.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Looking ahead, because of the state of the world, there is going to be many more foreign policy issues that are difficult, sensitive, prickly and controversial.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Israel-Hamas war is just the latest chapter.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Can you imagine if there is a war between the US and China or India and China or between our neighbours or in the South China Sea?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Then it would not be just economics or just emotion.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am very glad that our community and religious leaders have tried to help our people better understand the conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Trying to help people understand this conflict is a very dangerous and difficult exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I mean, you can ask the Ministry of Education (MOE) about this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am sure Minister Chan will explain more of that later on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, this is a wonderful example of Singapore unity, cohesion and compassion at its best.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think he said this in 1966, when speaking to some university students, "We must be realistic.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We cannot afford to indulge in emotional outbursts or in wishful thinking.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must face the hard facts of life and deal with them rationally and objectively." Mr Chairman, we have tried – in MFA and all our diplomats – to abide by this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, the conflict in Gaza is heart-breaking.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Every day, we are inundated with news and photos on TV as well as social media, portraying the violence committed upon innocent lives, including the elderly, babies, and children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The relentless destruction and humanitarian catastrophe is heart-wrenching.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The sadness and anxiety that we experience are part of our natural disposition as human beings who are driven to protect the vulnerable amongst us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As people with humanity and compassion, we reject all forms of injustice and cruelty.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As difficult it is for the eyes that see, it is even heavier for the shoulders that carry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also concerned that a potential ground offensive into Rafah will worsen the situation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The resolutions have condemned the attacks against all civilians and demanded that all parties comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the recent G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Brazil, I stressed our country’s firm position again.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Israel must step up to protect the safety and security of displaced civilians.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hamas needs to release all civilian hostages unconditionally and safely.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We know that this conflict is not an easy one to solve.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is a complex one that has dragged on for many years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have communicated this principled position on the international stage and through our voting record at the UNGA since 1967.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, we have voted in support of every UN resolution that calls on Israel to rescind all unilateral measures to change the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also opposed Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which are a violation of international law.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A two-state solution is the only way to stop the cycle of violence, and Singapore will do what we can to realise it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Singaporeans, we know that this is not a religious conflict.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is a struggle for territorial land that dates back centuries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, this issue has a deeper impact on Muslims around the world, including the Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Government understands that our community has specific ties towards this issue.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, the ties of kinship between our Muslim population and the Muslim population in Palestine.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, our ties towards the status of the Al-Aqsa Mosque, the third most important mosque for Muslims.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, our religious leaders have given guidance and space for our community to express all emotions, such as anger, pain and sympathy towards the suffering experienced by innocent victims, as well as hope for understanding and reconciliation between Israel and Palestine in a way that champions peace, and not destruction.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, the Office of the Mufti has issued a religious advisory which contains guidance on Islamic views towards violence and our reaction as believers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is in line with our vision of building and strengthening the Singapore Muslim Identity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Nevertheless, this does not mean it is only the Muslim community that is affected by the situation in Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many Singaporeans, regardless of race or religion, deeply sympathise with the plight of the Palestinians and the families of the hostages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They want to show their support in a constructive way.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Government has been working closely with community organisations to channel our energies towards concrete ways to help the victims of this tragedy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is heartening to see Singaporeans from all walks of life coming together to provide assistance, even until today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I want to assure Singaporeans that the Government is committed to continuing our humanitarian aid to Gaza, just as we have done in any crisis previously.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are working hard and closely collaborating with our partners in the Middle East to deliver aid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In November last year, I went to Cairo and witnessed the handover of these supplies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just a few weeks later, we deployed an RSAF aircraft to airlift humanitarian supplies as our second contribution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian has announced that we will soon donate a third tranche of aid for Gaza through Jordan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Apart from food supplies and medicine, we also sent a medical team to Egypt to treat casualties coming from Gaza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As we continue to help the victims of Gaza, a small fraction of society has questioned why we cannot take firmer measures against Israel.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, they want us to sever our diplomatic ties with Israel.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This issue relates directly to our foreign policy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Minister Vivian said, whatever action we take must prioritise our own national interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a small state, we remain relevant on the world stage by maintaining ties with as many countries as possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Breaking ties with those whose actions we disapprove of will not improve the situation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It would not change the tide of this conflict.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Even many countries in the Middle East such as Egypt, UAE and Jordan which are closer and more cognisant of the intricacies of this conflict have not severed ties with Israel.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But more importantly, Mr Chairman, keeping our ties does not mean that we are condoning their behaviour.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We voice this disagreement through our voting record for the UNGA resolutions on the Palestine issue as I explained earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, we want this conflict to end as soon as possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also want peace to be achieved as soon as possible so that the people on both sides can continue to live in safe and peaceful conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we acknowledge that the path to peace will not be easy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Currently, there is deep mistrust on both sides, and intra-Israeli and intra- Palestinian politics will further complicate the issue as both sides have conflicting positions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While this is not our quarrel, we have called on both sides to make the necessary compromises and commit to finding a solution in good faith.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, we should continue to ensure that events, even if they occur in distant places, do not threaten the stability and racial harmony that we experience here. : Mr Chairman, allow me to continue my speech in English.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today's fragmented world poses serious challenges for small states like us – that depend on inclusion, openness and a rules-based international architecture.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But this does not mean that we do not have agency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We can mitigate these concerns by enhancing our already strong ties with our web of partners and friends.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is not something that we are just doing now.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This work – of engagement; of making common cause; of forging mutually-beneficial partnerships – has been ongoing for years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will first speak about our immediate region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Keith Chua, Mr Don Wee, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Chong Kee Hiong, have asked about our relations with Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Around 30 Malaysian Ministers and senior officials visited Singapore in 2023 – including Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, who visited Singapore three times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To deepen mutual understanding and explore new areas of cooperation, our political officeholders also engaged at various state governments, including Penang, Johor, Selangor, Sarawak and Pahang.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I myself visited Kelantan and Terengganu in April 2023.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will increase as we find new ways to enhance cooperation and connectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both the SEZ and RTS are testament to our extensive people-to-people ties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: High-level engagements have been regular, with both President Jokowi and Vice-President Ma'ruf Amin visiting in 2023.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We continue to build ties at the regional level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I had the chance to visit North Sumatra, Aceh and the Riau Islands last year, where I met political and religious leaders, businesses and students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are focusing on new areas of cooperation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, we signed an MOU last year to set up the Singapore-Indonesia Tech:X programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We thank President Jokowi for his efforts in deepening bilateral ties and we look forward to engaging the incoming administration in the same positive way.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There are complementarities between Singapore and Indonesia, so there is still much more that we can do together for mutual benefit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We can continue to explore cooperation at the central and regional levels, in areas like education, human capital development and emerging sectors like in energy and sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our special relationship with Brunei continues to grow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the leadership level, ties are very close.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lawrence Wong co-led the 9th Young Leaders' Programme with His Royal Highness Crown Prince Haji Al-Muhtadee Billah in Brunei in December 2023.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The President visited Brunei last month in his first state visit since taking office.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the same month, our Prime Minister, Senior Minister Teo and Minister Vivian also attended Prince Abdul Mateen's wedding.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are committed to deepening people-to-people ties through initiatives like the Brunei Darussalam – Singapore Youth Education Scholarship programme and the MOU on Strengthening Civil Service Cooperation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are celebrating the 40th anniversary of diplomatic ties with Brunei this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The 4G leadership remains committed to maintaining this special relationship.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to exploring more ways to advance our cooperation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This includes new and emerging areas like the green economy, renewable energy, food and medical supply resilience and digital connectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Wee and Mr Nair asked about our relations with the rest of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We celebrated the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations with Vietnam last year and are exploring the possibility of upgrading relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will celebrate the 50th anniversary of relations with Laos and our 55th anniversary with the Philippines this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are closely engaging the new governments in Cambodia and Thailand, with whom we will be celebrating the 60th anniversary of relations next year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Nair and Mr Dennis Tan have noted, the situation there is grave and the level of displacement and humanitarian suffering, concerning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to support ASEAN's efforts to provide humanitarian assistance through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN will continue to address the Myanmar issue in line with the Five-Point Consensus (5PC).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is unfortunate that there has been limited progress in the implementation of the 5PC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we recognise that the situation in Myanmar is complicated and will take a long time to resolve.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Any enduring political solution will have to come from within Myanmar itself.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That said, we are committed to working with our partners to facilitate peace and national reconciliation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is in our interest to have a stable and conducive regional environment to attract businesses and investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Tan asked how Singapore can help uphold regional stability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One way is through our consistent bilateral engagements at the leadership level as the earlier generation of leaders did as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Several of our neighbours have had recent leadership transitions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we have good links with many of them over the years and we will continue to work closely with them to foster regional stability and prosperity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN forms the cornerstone of our open, inclusive and rules-based regional architecture.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Its success is critical to the success of all its members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if ASEAN would require reforms or a bigger budget to be a more effective organisation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will ensure that the ASEAN Secretariat is adequately resourced so that they can fulfil their functions and support the region's needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is as ASEAN also takes steps to strengthen itself and introduce more effective work processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Lim and Mr Liang Eng Hwa have asked how ASEAN would be able to maintain its relevance in today's geopolitical environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, ASEAN Centrality has become even more important in the face of intensifying intra-ASEAN challenges and major power rivalry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our priority now is the implementation of the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Under the AOIP, we are exploring concrete projects with our partners in four priority areas: economy, maritime cooperation, connectivity, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through these projects, we aim to increase ASEAN's mindshare, promote mutual benefit, and keep external partners vested in the stability of our region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN is a region of considerable economic opportunity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I would encourage younger Singaporeans to consider doing their internships or a semester abroad in an ASEAN country.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN provides a platform for economic cooperation and integration.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, the region is committed to addressing climate change and transitioning to a green economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat last month, there was discussion about ASEAN's Power Grid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The benefits of a power grid will be enormous in terms of energy accessibility, decarbonisation and economic opportunity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We signed a Green-Digital Economic Partnership agreement with Vietnam last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We were the first to sign a Letter of Intent with Indonesia on cross-border carbon capture and storage (CCS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also exploring carbon credits collaboration with Laos.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN has launched negotiations on the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which we aim to settle this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore has digital payment links with Thailand and Malaysia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, we launched a cross-border QR payment linkage with Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are seeking to pursue similar arrangements at the multilateral level through ASEAN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the 2024 ASEAN chair, Laos has decided on the theme "Enhancing Connectivity and Resilience".

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recognise that Laos' ASEAN chairmanship comes at a crucial time, as ASEAN seeks to position itself for future growth amidst global headwinds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The creation of more shared opportunities in areas like connectivity, supply chains, and energy resilience will benefit all ASEAN members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also looking to deepen engagements with partners outside of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to grow our relations with South Asia, which is a key region for us given our proximity, economic links and history.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Edward Chia asked about our relations with India.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India is one of our key partners in South Asia and a rising global economic power.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have had a slew of high-level engagements, especially during India's G20 presidency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To Mr Neil's query on the Gulf States, we enjoy good ties with many of them and are seeking further collaboration in areas like trade and investment, digital governance, cybersecurity and low-carbon energy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will provide an enhanced platform for us to deepen cooperation in mutually beneficial areas like human capital development and halal industry cooperation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have sustained high-level engagement with our African partners too.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Wee asked about the ties between Singapore and South Africa.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, we have kept up engagements at the leadership level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian hosted the 4th Singapore-Sub-Saharan Africa High-Level Ministerial Exchange Visit in August 2023.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: South Africa Deputy President Paul Mashatile made an official visit to Singapore in December 2023.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to bolster ties with our African friends and look for ways to strengthen economic and people-to-people exchanges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Liang, Mr Alex Yam and Ms Nadia Ahmad Sadin have asked what role Singapore can play to support international order.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We can do so by remaining a staunch advocate for rules-based multilateralism.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many other nations see us as a consistent and constructive player on the international stage, evident in the election results of our candidatures in organisations like the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the International Maritime Organization (IMO).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will try to contribute to the shaping of global norms in a positive way.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas asked how Singapore has been engaging multilateral groups to prepare for common challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are the founder and remain the convener of the Forum of Small States (FOSS) at the UN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just last week, we hosted the UN Permanent Representatives under the 12th FOSS Fellowship Programme, to discuss best practices on issues like sustainable development, climate change, cybersecurity and digital transformation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I have talked about some of our bilateral and multilateral relations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will elaborate on other accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But the main point is this: it is our ties with the rest of the world that will help put us in a position to thrive even in turbulent times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is what our officers here and in overseas missions have been working hard on.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MFA will continue to play our part in safeguarding our survival and fostering our prosperity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Minister Vivian has explained why Singapore’s foreign policy has to be driven by the long-term interests of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are a small country with no hinterland, no natural resources, and no intrinsic relevance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have an open and trade-based economy that is vulnerable to external developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are a multiracial, multi-religious and multilingual society in the heart of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our foreign policy cannot be driven by prevailing sentiments or affinity to any external group, however powerfully felt they might be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It must be based on understanding our core interests and acting consistently, in accordance with the principles that safeguard Singapore’s independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The conflict that has raged in Gaza between Israel and Hamas since October 2023 has attracted much attention around the world, and demonstrates how Singapore’s approach towards foreign policy will be tested again and again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To many in the Chinese-speaking community in Singapore, the Israel-Hamas conflict is part of the long-standing and complex troubles in the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The historical threads of who should be blamed for doing what to whom are difficult to sort out – as the Chinese saying goes, you cannot slice through the knots, and the more you try to detangle, the worse the knots become (剪不断、理还乱).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This view is reflected from the reports and commentaries on the subject carried in our Chinese-language media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But, for not a few of our fellow Singaporeans, this is a massive and tragic catastrophe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Israel’s military response to Hamas’s horrific acts of terrorism of 7 October 2023 has resulted in mass civilian casualties and a humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with women and children among the worst affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is not at all an exaggeration to say that those of our fellow Singaporeans who care deeply about the Gaza issue find it hard to sleep and eat in peace, and experience great pain and anguish (寝食难安、痛心疾首).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This has led to calls for Singapore to do more on the foreign policy front to show solidarity with the Palestinians in Gaza and condemn Israel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Vivian and Second Minister Maliki have addressed the Government’s position in their speeches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It was a blatant and abhorrent act of terrorism that cannot be justified by any circumstances, context or history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Terrorism poses a clear and present threat to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To excuse terrorism now would endanger Singapore in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is not because we are taking sides.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Israel’s conduct must abide by the principles of necessity and proportionality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also concerned that a potential ground offensive into Rafah will worsen the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, we also call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We call for negotiations toward a two-state solution consistent with relevant UNSC resolutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the only option for a durable peace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is not the first or the last time when some Singaporeans would feel the powerful pull of sentiments arising from events happening beyond our shores, and call for our foreign policy to reflect these sentiments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It will also not be the last time when sentiments felt strongly by one group of Singaporeans are not necessarily shared to the same extent by others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are, after all, a diverse society – made up of fellow citizens from different ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This diversity is a great strength for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But our ever-present challenge is to maintain unity of purpose while amidst diversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the case of foreign policy, it is about ensuring that our foreign policy always reflects Singapore’s core interests, despite the ebbs and flows of sentiments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain, Mr Edward Chia and Ms Tin Pei Ling have asked about how Singapore can remain vigilant against foreign interference in domestic politics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are a diverse society who lives in harmony.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We enjoy mutual respect and a shared sense of national purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is an achievement to be proud of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This has given us a richness of perspective and experience that has been an advantage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our diversity also means that external forces can try to divide us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There have been attempts to condition us to think in certain ways by appealing to a more specific racial or religious identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is why the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act (FICA) was introduced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: FICA is aimed at protecting the integrity of our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The recent case where an individual was designated as a politically significant person (PSP) for the first time under the FICA brings this issue to the fore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This development has raised questions within some segments of the Chinese community over the parameters, which businesses and civic groups can engage foreign organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As FICA comes under the ambit of MHA, I will not discuss the operationalisation of the Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, I would like to make three points from MFA’s perspective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we recognise that the Chinese community in Singapore embodies the tradition of 忧国忧民 - caring not just about their own success but that of the entire nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore Chinese civic and business leaders are fully aware of the importance of effective diplomacy to Singapore, and tend to watch developments in our external relations closely and contribute actively to discourse on Singapore’s foreign policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many Singapore Chinese community leaders have been generous in sharing their experiences and insights in doing business and dealing with officials overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, those who wish to contribute to flying Singapore’s flag need to develop a good understanding of our core interests, which is underpinned by promoting a just, inclusive and rules-based international order where sovereign states, regardless of size, have equal rights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Vivian has expounded on this in his COS speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have taken pains, for example, during the debate on the Addendum to the President’s Address last April, to highlight that our foreign policy is not premised on neutrality or seeking to balance between big powers, but on Singapore’s core interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These interests are founded on our identity as multiracial country, representing all Singaporeans regardless of race.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ethnic connections are useful in cultivating business and friendships wigion, but fundamentally, we look at things as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When speaking, we must speak as Singaporeans, on behalf of multiracial Singapore, even when dealing with countries with whom we have very close and friendly relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, cultural affinity does not equate national identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Take Singaporeans of Chinese ethnic descent for instance – we are both Singaporeans and Singaporean Chinese (huaren), but not overseas Chinese (huaqiao).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members of the Singapore Chinese community, civic organisations and business associations that grasp the above points fully would be able to play an effective role as we seek to build win-win international partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Even amidst a world that is increasingly polarised, Singapore can, and does, maintain excellent relations with all our major partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, we maintain very good ties with the US and China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Both of them continue to work with us because they trust that we continue to act in a principled, open and consistent manner, based on our long-term national interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Edward Chia have asked about Singapore’s outlook for China in 2024 and how we can build up our bilateral relations with China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have good relations at the leadership level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past year, we welcomed PRC Vice President Han Zheng and Foreign Minister Wang Yi to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Prime Minister Lee, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Minister Vivian and several other Singaporean leaders, including myself, have visited China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our people-to-people ties have also been strong due to, inter alia, our extensive business links, student exchanges and tourism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The recent entry into force of the 30-day mutual visa exemption arrangement provides more opportunities for those ties to deepen and broaden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Relations are anchored by the Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC), which is the apex bilateral cooperation platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is growing cooperation in traditional areas like trade, finance and people-to-people exchanges, as well as in emerging areas like the digital and green economies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As the world’s second largest economy and our largest trading partner in goods, there are significant opportunities for us to cooperate with China economically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to explore ways to further broaden our engagement of China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such achievements in our bilateral relations do not stem from the individual initiatives, but rather, comes from strong links between our governments, peoples and businesses which have been built up over many decades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government will continue to work hard at identifying ways through which we can forge deeper people-to-people ties and friendships with China. : Mr Henry Kwek asked how Singapore can remain a trusted partner of the US.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore has a deep and dynamic partnership with the US – spanning the economic, trade, security and defence spheres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Economic relations have grown significantly since the establishment of the US-Singapore FTA, the first between the US and an Asian country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are expanding cooperation with the US in emerging areas like technology and innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We launched the US-Singapore Critical and Emerging Technology Dialogue last October.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are working with the US to develop a roadmap for our digital economic cooperation to chart common principles in areas like digital standards, consumer protection and data governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also looking to strengthen cooperation on climate resilient infrastructure and regional decarbonisation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, I seek your indulgence for a few more minutes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Dennis Tan spoke about intensifying US-China competition.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As partners with both, we are heartened to see that their relations have improved over the past few months.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We expect that tensions between the two countries will persist for some time and competition will be inevitable to some degree.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But this does not mean that the entire relationship has to be zero-sum.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: There are still many areas, where both sides can work together for mutual benefit and for the global good.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This could include climate change, macroeconomic stability, global health and food security.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It could also extend to emerging areas – like AI governance and safety.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Zhulkarnain, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Shawn Huang asked how Singapore is building relations with other countries, including new and emerging markets, to enhance our economic and supply chain resilience.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We are deepening our links with other significant global players.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Japan and the Republic of Korea are strong economic partners and fellow champions of an open trading system.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We continue to strengthen cooperation with both in new areas, like the digital and green economies, energy transition and sustainability.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This will provide enhanced access to the UK market and new opportunities for trade and investment for Singapore companies.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We are looking at new avenues of cooperation with the EU.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Closer to our region, we continue to refresh our engagements with our longstanding strategic partner – Australia.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have complementary strengths and an interest, increasing cooperation in supply chain resilience, renewable energy and the digital and green economies and we will also focus more on emerging markets further afield.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Ms Rachel Ong, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and Mr Mark Lee asked how MFA can engage Singaporeans and businesses on foreign policy issues amidst global uncertainties.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have stated earlier, that unity and cohesion are prerequisites if we are to navigate an increasingly dangerous and contested world.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Minister Vivian, Second Minister Maliki and I, along with other Ministers, Ambassadors and senior MFA officials, spend time speaking to students and members of the public.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We value Singaporeans' views on global affairs and embrace the opportunity to discuss foreign policy considerations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also do the same with business leaders and chambers of commerce and industry.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: They, too, are keen to understand Singapore's assessment of the global geopolitical situation and the risks and opportunities that arise from it.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The intention is to create a broad understanding of the principles and motivations that underlie our foreign policy.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Hopefully, this can lead to consensus on the way forward.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But even if that is elusive, we must be able to calmly agree to disagree.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We must not let external issues or external forces divide us.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: If we can achieve this, then we can continuously exercise our agency and find ways to keep Singapore safe and thriving.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is for the sake of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, thank you to the Minister for a very broad-ranging speech which I thought was very helpful.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I refer to one of the points which he anchored his speech on, which is about foreign policy beginning at home and the importance of a cohesive and united society in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Perhaps, it is best to describe it through something which happened some years ago.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It does not matter which country it is, it does not matter which race or which Embassy it was.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A particular Embassy had reached out to Singaporean MPs of a particular race and had invited them for an event.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And it did not take long, in fact, hardly a few seconds for me to just tell the Minister, "Look, I think that is something we will follow suit because we are Singapore." I think that is something quite pregnant with meaning to it when I said that, when I said, "We are Singapore." I want to share this episode just to set the tone of the conversation in the right spirit.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have no disagreement with the Minister about how important it is for Singapore to retain our right to self defence.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The only issue in case of Israel-Hama's conflict was that the conflict had a history.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I do not mean a long history, but I mean a far shorter history – four conflicts in a short period of about less than two decades.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Almost every time, it is a case of one side going too far.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And this was what I sought to share in my speech in November when Mr Vikram Nair and his colleagues filed a Motion on this subject.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second element which I think is important to talk about and the Minister made the nuance actually very well in his speech when he talked about the events of 7 October.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The only issue, Sir, is language shapes narrative.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In a conflict, that is critical insofar as shaping minds and shaping the information landscape and when you have a situation where one party is likely to dehumanise another party – which they have done in the past; its senior leadership, people in government continue to do so – the language that is used is important.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I recall the Minister in November, being very careful and he said, "Notice I am just referring to what happened on that day." I think that is important.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Those are the points that I feel compelled to share with the Minister notwithstanding my broad agreement with what he has shared today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But I have two questions that can be helpful in terms of the public conversation and in terms of engagement with Singaporeans on foreign policy.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One, again, on the Israel-Hamas issue, I have received those emails.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I am sure the Ministry has received those emails.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I cannot speak for every email that comes through.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think a few of their ministers have said so publicly, notwithstanding a motion that was passed in the Israeli parliament last week.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, it will be helpful to understand how we traverse, how we move on a foreign policy issue, when we take a particular position and one of the other parties takes a diametrically different position.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Singh, I would appreciate if you could keep your clarification short.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This was also a similar question that came up arising from our activities on the ground.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am not putting these questions to suggest that I disagree with the position of MFA on these matters, but that understanding is something that can move the conversation in public forward, because as the Minister has also shared, a lot of people in Singapore are talking about it for various reasons.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, I will thank the Member for his cooperation in the past.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member has highlighted the danger of words used or misused, or used without sufficient thought or caution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the Member has also highlighted the dangers of dehumanising someone whom you do not agree with.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On this, I can say I agree with you on those points.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am saying I detect that, actually, the Member is agreeing with us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Chairman, can I just seek confirmation that the Member agrees with us?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But the point I think was about how you respond when the other party actually takes a diametrically different position from your national position.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Chairman, I will interpret that as, actually, the Member agrees.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But the Member's question, to be fair, is please share what is the Member's thinking behind.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because the WP and the PAP can arrive at the same decision, but for completely different reasons and a different rationale.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I think it is a fair question to seek what are your principal considerations and how do you arrive at a decision like this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I cannot recall a single moment when we have broken ties.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that is just a matter of fact-checking.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, to the question, from time to time, will we have disagreements, even stand-offs, even close to kinetic action with other countries?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And will a performative gesture of formally breaking ties, would that necessarily be helpful?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that would be my first question that I would ask myself and I would ask my staff and I would ask the Prime Minister.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Do we want to go through this performative gesture and will it help?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My own inclination is to say, in times of tensions, in times of divergence, in times of conflict, the more you can engage and communicate and keep multiple channels of communication open, the better.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, without spilling state secrets, have I continued to meet informally my counterpart in Russia?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have told my Prime Minister I have had to inhale second-hand smoke and I have drunk good whiskey for the sake of Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because I am not engaged in performative gestures.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the same time, I want to communicate to him and to his country, so they know why we had taken a different position from them.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I can say that our relations with Russia, I mean, the Russians have had to say certain things about us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, in fact, if you observe their acts, the actions and the conduct between Russia and Singapore, it has been mutually respectful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I look forward to the day when the war in Ukraine ends, and relations and the conduct of business can get back to normal.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Coming to Israel, it has been a rare privilege that our diplomats and Ministers have access to all the countries, literally, all the countries in the Middle East, even and especially during this time of crisis.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We do not agree with everything that every counterpart in Israel and the Arab countries state, but they listen to us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And mind you, even for the delivery of humanitarian assistance, we will need to work with Israel.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The fact that everyone knows we do have good relations with Israel also gives us a special ability to contribute and to be more effective in the delivery of humanitarian assistance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There will be disagreements from time to time, that is normal.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having more channels open in general is good.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Do you have to, sometimes, take actions to signify your disapproval?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But even in your choice of actions and diplomatic gestures, be very restrained, be very careful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we have an opinion – for what it is worth.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Both the Israelis and the Palestinians know our position is not identical with each of them, but they know why we take the positions that we take, and that has not stopped us from having mutually respectful and constructive relations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: No, I do not take it for granted.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When I share notes, even with my counterparts in ASEAN, in other countries, very few people have access that we have had.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have been to Jerusalem, to literally every capital.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When we went to Jerusalem, and the Prime Minister will recall, the way in which the Israelis, the Jordanians, the administrators of Al-Haram, Al-Sharif, the way they treated us and the access that they gave us, the Prime Minister will agree, it was unprecedented.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think we had that because we have conducted foreign policy in a principled, consistent, respectful and constructive way for decades.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And that gives us access, that gives us some relevance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The purpose of most of my speech today was not about the technicalities of foreign policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Actually, it is to reflect that our very foundation and our identity is based on diversity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is our identity, it is our strength, but also understand that with that strength comes portals of vulnerabilities.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we will still make common cause and we will still be constructive partners with our friends across conflict zones.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Whether that conflict is in Myanmar, which is a civil war; between neighbours like Ukraine and Russia, who also have a complicated history; or between the interminable rounds of violence in the Middle East.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The fact that Singapore is, well, you know, has access, has respect and has a small and constructive role to play is something which we should be grateful for.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But my main point today, so long as we stay united, so long as we are able to respect, truly respect diverse opinions and still operate as a united whole.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I see many Members wanting to seek clarifications, which is good.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The last clarification was six minutes long; so I want to make sure we keep it short.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Mr Chairman, sir, may I seek a response to my cut speech on improving consular services for Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Chairman, thank you for the opportunity to address Mr Murali and I believe also Mr Xie Yao Quan's cut, on how MFA has leveraged technology to improve our consular services.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: One of the most important roles for MFA is to provide consular assistance to Singaporeans who are abroad.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The volume is growing as more Singaporeans live, work and travel abroad.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: A Document of Identity is a temporary travel document for Singaporeans who have lost their passports and which enables them to return home.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To mitigate this, we continue to build a pool of professional first responders in MFA headquarters, who can render 24/7 consular support and assistance to Singaporeans overseas via phone and email.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Murali has asked how MFA assesses Singaporeans' satisfaction with consular services rendered to them.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We place great importance on such feedback that we receive from members of the public.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We are encouraged by positive feedback that we have regularly received from citizens, but we continue to actively evaluate comments and suggestions on areas that we can improve on.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will also use this data to analyse trends and thereby sharpen our ability to deliver timely assistance.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: While I appreciate the Minister taking great pains to explain and address concerns, reiterating some of Singapore's positions regarding acts of terrorism, the votes we have taken at UN and correctly reminding us of our fragile place in the world and the importance of unity among our people, all of which I agree with, and while I can also understand Minister's explanation as to why we have not cut off ties, including with Israel, because at the end of the day, bearing in mind our size, maybe having a seat at the table and a chance to dialogue is better than closing off the chance to raise concerns.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: And also how our aid is trustworthy, our medical supplies are what they say they are, and are more likely be able to pass through borders.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: The question I have, Sir, which many on the ground also have is, how are we translating our position that, according to the Minister in this case, maybe Israel has gone too far and that we are supportive of a ceasefire to prevent further humanitarian tragedy in Gaza, to how foreign policy begins at home in a congruent manner across all of Government – for example, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) in the case of permits for events, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) for dialogues, MOE for the way we educate our students and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) in the case of the Air Show.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Chair, I do not think it is appropriate for me to respond on behalf of MHA or MOE, so, let me try to confine my answer to MFA.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, I thank the Member for her understanding and agreement with the elements of our foreign policy that I have expounded on.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Specifically, the question on how our stand, given that it differs from the Israelis, because I am sure the Israelis will disagree with us, I think, when we say that the military response has gone too far.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Similarly, in my conversations with my Arab counterparts, their interpretation of events will not be identical to ours.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I would say the first point is to accept that these differences are in the nature of things.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What has been good is that it has not stopped us from communicating, from working together and in the more specific case now of even delivering humanitarian assistance and more to come.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am glad, therefore, that the Member agrees, particularly that we should not break ties and we should maintain those links, despite the differences of opinion that we have.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What we are witnessing, frankly, is a cynical calculus in blood.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we do not want any part of that, because we are not party to that quarrel.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we are simply taking a stand on principle: terrorism is wrong, hostage-taking is wrong, please release the hostages immediately, do not use any excuse historical or whatever to cover for that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the same time, two wrongs do not make a right.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Even when you pursue self defence, there are limits and please stay within those limits.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the end of it all, remember despite all the diversity in the world and even the discordance, we are all human beings and we must feel something for innocent civilians.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Every innocent child, every civilian who loses his life or has a family member maimed, this is in fact storing up tinder for the next cycle of violence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, even if you want to take a completely amoral attitude to this calculus, this is counterproductive.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, I reiterate that I am very grateful for, I believe, the consensus that we have achieved here and it enables me to speak to my counterparts with greater confidence that I have the support of Members in this House and of Singaporeans when we pursue a foreign policy that is principle-based, that is consistent, that is constructive and that is able to operate in the midst of diversity, both internally and externally, the same.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Our relations with the middle powers are increasingly more important as we navigate the complexities of today's global order.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The first is as regards to the EU-Singapore Trade Agreement, there are two subsidiary agreements, the EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement and the EU-Singapore Partnership and Cooperation Agreement which have yet to be ratified.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Could I ask the Senior Minister of State if she could give some updates on what is the status of that and when we can expect them to be ratified and come into force.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The second is as regard our ties with Germany, Federal Chancellor Olaf Scholz and Prime Minister issued a joint declaration in 2022 entitled Partners for a Resilient and Sustainable Future which included enhancing cooperation in various economic areas.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I am not able to give a timeframe, but this is something that we regularly bring up with our EU member state counterparts whenever we meet them.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also share close defence ties and this existing foundation enables us, I believe, to collaborate more effectively on new and emerging areas such as sustainability and innovation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to clarify, what is the significance of this move now and is it in any way related to 7 October, or is it part of a longer-term strategy?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The timing of our resident ambassador taking up post had nothing to do with 7 October.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It was just fortuitous or unfortuitous, depending on your point of view.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The answer is yes, it was part of a longer-term plan.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Beyond the travails that Israel has gone through, if you just stop thinking about the conflict but just look at their achievements economically, their achievements technologically, especially in cyber, in water, in agriculture and in many of the advanced technologies, it is a place with talent and technologies that we want access to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As the Member said, our diplomatic ties with them go back a long time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we do not have enough people to place all over the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Right now, in terms of ambassadors, resident ambassadors, I think the number is just around 40.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you include all the consulates, we have maybe about 50-odd consulates in the world, in a world with about 200 states!

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the short answer to the question is, it had everything to do with long-term plans and long-term opportunities.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: I just want to come back to my cut about how Singapore is helping other countries to build capacity.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Can I seek some clarification from MFA, please?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For example, we are working more with the Pacific Islands, who are fellow small island developing states.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Minister Vivian attended the 52nd Pacific Islands Forum Leaders' Meeting in November 2023.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is a customised three-year programme that aims to help the Pacific community build capacity to address some of the most pressing challenges that they have identified.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: The first supplementary question is that there seems to be an increasing demand amongst young people to be more involved in engaging and hearing out their views.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: Therefore, I was wondering if MFA would consider getting young people involved by developing youth leaders, pardon my pun, as ambassadors on the ground, as well as creating more spaces for organised discussion so that MFA can thoroughly explain their policy formulation.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: My second supplementary question is in regards to what Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said yesterday about nurturing, supporting and providing more Singaporeans who wish to go overseas to work and grow their experience.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: How does MFA actually plan to support and provide reassurance to Singaporeans working and living overseas, particularly during this volatile global landscape, in ensuring their safety and well-being so that we can inspire confidence among these Singaporeans and families to pursue their global opportunities boldly, knowing that the Ministry has their back?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On the first point, I agree with the Member.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Young Singaporeans have views and they do want to have access to the facts, the narratives, and I think they do want to have spaces for structured discussions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But particularly, when you are dealing with a live issue, it becomes that much harder, not just in terms of urgency but because emotions are raw, the chief protagonists are still in play – and it is not possible always to have a dispassionate remote discussion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Frankly, I think in the past, in a pre-social-media age and the Internet, it was easier to say: wait a minute, this is still a live issue, let us give it some time; and then discuss it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not think that option is available today because if we do not actually provide safe places for structured discussions, and deliberately try to lower temperatures and have discussions that shed more light than heat, what will happen in the absence of that is you will see the unbridled and sometimes unhinged, unfair and inaccurate portrayals in social media dominating.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I just want to say I agree with you, and it is in that spirit, and again I am not speaking on behalf of Minister Chan, but it is in that spirit we have to support the efforts of MOE, MHA, the Ministry for Culture, Community and Youth in the months and years to come.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We need to do far more than we used to do in the past.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second point is, you will be amazed at how widely and well-travelled Singaporeans are.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I get to know about it when they get into trouble and a phone call comes or a message, an email comes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the first point is Singaporeans are some of the most widely travelled people in the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Good because first, Singaporeans have opportunities; two, because Singaporeans are also broadening their minds and horizons and are looking for opportunities overseas, and the fact that you are Singaporean with the red passport, one of the most accessible passports in the world, that is a strength.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having said that, I must also confess to sometimes being worried when Singaporeans then turn around and say: I need you to give me a warranty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the answer is: yes, I do have your back and I will do my best, but I cannot give you a warranty that the rest of the world is as safe and secure and peaceful as Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: During those rare occasions when MFA actually issues a travel advisory or travel notice, I appeal for Singaporeans, please pay attention to it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Do not go to a trouble spot if you really do not have to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And in any case, if you do, for whatever reason, please register with us and we will do our best.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that is another plug for ASEAN and why we must get into this habit of looking out for each other.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If there are no further clarifications, can I invite Mr Vikram Nair if you would like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think in a slightly unusual approach, all three addressing the Israel-Hamas issue, which is an emotive issue.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But I think it has been good that we have the position of the Government explained clearly.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am also grateful to the Leader of the Opposition for standing with us on this difficult issue.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Since we have consensus, Chairman, I seek your leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.05 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 3.42 pm until 4.05 pm.
